findings.rotation: OpenStax vertebral-joints discussion: lumbar facets largely prohibit rotation; the thoracic cage limits flexion and other motions. It does not specify the exact endpoints used here.
findings.external_oblique: Costal digitations arise on ribs 5–12. Elongated lateral fleshy belly transitions anteriorly into a broad aponeurosis; anterior fibers are predominantly inferior-medial, posterior fibers descend toward the iliac crest more vertically.
findings.internal_oblique: Intermediate layer; fibers predominantly superior and medial; displayed through a cutaway.
findings.serratus_anterior: Costal slips on ribs 1–8 or 1–9 converge toward the costal surface of the medial scapular border. Upper slips are partly covered by pectoral context.
findings.rectus_abdominis: Paired muscle from pubic crest/symphysis toward xiphoid and upper costal cartilages; linea alba and three tendinous intersections.
findings.latissimus_dorsi: Broad posterior lower-thoracic/thoracolumbar-fascial/iliac origin converges to the posterior axillary fold and proximal humeral context. Humerus is omitted. The upper end is below the shoulder joint and the iliac origin is stationary. Opaque visibility is derived from the curved surface facing the camera; posterior serratus is partly overlapped.
findings.pectoral_context: Compact curved anterior chest fan with fibers converging to the anterior axillary fold/proximal humeral context. Sternum and pectoral context share a frame; near/far fans are sorted after deformation.

illustrative_choices.limits: No subject-specific measurements, muscle sliding, activation, pressure or clinical joint/contact simulation. SVG layers depict anatomical overlap; this is not a volumetric dissection renderer.
illustrative_choices.upper_thorax_plateau: T1–T4 shoulder/rib-cage block; remaining thoracic rotation distributed below; an illustrative coupling constraint, not clinical regional motion data
illustrative_choices.yaw_axis: Fixed pelvic longitudinal axis; vertebral centerline curvature rotates with the torso

visual_guide.description: User-approved colored concept in this chat guided the silhouette and separation of external-oblique belly/aponeurosis. The user supplied a separate dissection reference for that relationship. The generated concept is not used as anatomical ground truth.

recheck.reason: Previous coordinate/opacity checks did not verify attachment topology or anatomical silhouettes. This recheck compares textbook figure 1112, 1118 and 1119 directly with the rendered front/lateral/yaw plates.
observed_errors: EO drawn as a narrow lateral strip with unrelated costal teeth
SA front insertion assigned anterior depth instead of costal scapular surface
Latissimus modeled as a long strap ending at shoulder-joint height rather than proximal humeral context
Pectoral sternocostal origin cut off above lower costal cartilages
Generic height deformation let muscle origins move differently from corresponding rigid ribs
Torso width changed discontinuously at y=345 and y=410, producing fiber kinks
corrections: UV attachment patches wrap around a smooth torso width/depth profile
SA origins ribs 1–8 follow each rib; insertions follow costal medial scapular border
EO origins ribs 5–12 include posterior lower costal branches; anterior belly joins broad aponeurosis and posterior fibers approach iliac crest
Latissimus broad lower-thoracic/fascial/iliac origins converge to omitted proximal humeral context; iliac origin stays fixed
Pectoral fan includes inferior sternocostal extent and ends below shoulder joint
Back-facing mesh cells and fiber segments are excluded from opaque rendering; transparent groups reveal the complete sheet
recheck.verification_scope: Attachment probes compare to actual rendered rib polylines, not just to the deformation function. Tests establish drawing consistency, not an anatomically validated volumetric model or clinical range of motion.
